issues.description: Method Milkable.messageOnMilk(): the problem statement (UML and textual requirements) declares messageOnMilk() as returning a String and specifies it should return the text "[Animal Type] [name] is milked". The solution repository defines the interface method as returning boolean (boolean messageOnMilk()) and the Goat and Seal implementations print the milk message to stdout and return true. This return-type mismatch between the specification (String) and the solution code (boolean) creates a compile-time / design conflict and will confuse students about whether to implement/return a String or a boolean and whether to print or return the milk message.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix: change the interface and implementations in the solution to match the problem statement: update Milkable.java to 'String messageOnMilk();' and modify Goat.messageOnMilk() and Seal.messageOnMilk() to return the string "Goat [name] is milked" and "Seal [name] is milked" respectively (do not print inside these methods). Alternatively, if the intended design is to return boolean, update the problem statement (UML and textual description) to declare messageOnMilk() returns boolean and explicitly document that implementations print the milk message and return true/false.
